entries.surface: `Capabilities-Etag` response header on GET /.well-known/openwop
entries.authority: RFC 0165 §C.2: hosts SHOULD send a standard ETag on /.well-known/openwop and honor If-None-Match; Capabilities-Etag keeps its semantics through v1.x and is removed at 2.0
entries.replacement: standard `ETag` / `If-None-Match` on the discovery document (dual-emitted through v1.x)
entries.note: RFC 0176 §C.2: absent from the v2 representation at the cut; removed from the v1 representation at v1 end-of-support.

entries.surface: capabilities `contractProvenance` root block ({ suiteVersion, corpusCommit })
entries.authority: v2 charter program C.2 (proposal only; RFC 0146 added the block and no RFC has deprecated it)
entries.replacement: `protocolVersions[]` for contract level; `host.build.{kind,id}` in certification bundle v3 for build identity
entries.note: Proposed because the block is an advisory self-declaration the wire cannot falsify (its own description says it is NOT an integrity check).

entries.surface: the `X-openwop-*` webhook delivery header family (Webhook-Id, Event-Type, Timestamp, Signature, Signature-Algorithm)
entries.authority: RFC 0165 §C.1: hosts SHOULD dual-emit the `OpenWOP-*` family with identical values; subscribers SHOULD accept either; the `X-openwop-*` family MUST still be sent through v1.x and is removed at 2.0
entries.note: The un-prefixed `{hex}` signature value was corrected in place (INTEROP-MATRIX 2026-08-24), not deprecated. The SDKs' `openwop-Webhook-Signature: v1=` header appears in no spec file and is an SDK-versus-spec defect fixed in openwop-sdks alongside RFC 0165 (helpers verify OpenWOP-Signature, then X-openwop-Signature, then the legacy name).

entries.surface: `409 interrupt_already_resolved` (interrupt.md) and `410 interrupt_gone` (interrupt-profiles.md) for an invalidated interrupt token
entries.authority: v2 charter program C.4 (error registry): one code per condition
entries.replacement: one registered code for "token invalidated", chosen by the C.4 child RFC
entries.note: Not a deprecation today: both codes are live and normative in different documents for overlapping conditions (a token invalidated by resolution or cancel). Recorded here so the overlap is not lost before the error registry decides it.

entries.surface: `engineVersion` typed integer at the discovery root and string on run-event / run-snapshot / three event payloads
entries.authority: RFC 0165 §A.4 (recorded; unification is a v2 C.5 item — changing either type is a COMPATIBILITY §2.2 break in v1.x)
entries.note: In v1.x the per-event value is the decimal string rendering of the root integer (version-negotiation.md §"Protocol version grammar").

entries.surface: `since` query parameter on GET /v1/runs/{runId}/events/poll
entries.authority: v2 charter C.4 (RFC 0167 §E; version-negotiation.md names `lastSequence` authoritative and `since` back-compat for pre-v1.0 deployments)
entries.replacement: `lastSequence` in v1.x; the v2 C.4 child defines the cursor (RFC 0165 G7)
entries.note: Proposed: the prose tolerates `since` without an RFC or annotation, so there is nothing to cite as a v1.x deprecation; the v2 cut removes it with the cursor redefinition.

entries.surface: `X-Dedup`, `X-Force-Engine-Version`, `X-Pack-Sha`, `X-Pack-Signing-Method` request headers
entries.authority: v2 charter C.4 (RFC 0167 §E): `OpenWOP-*` for every non-standard header; RFC 0165 §C.1 covered only the webhook family
entries.note: Proposed: the four surviving `X-` request headers on canonical or seam operations; renamed by the C.4 child under the one-header-scheme rule.

entries.surface: the 11 `§host.*` families RFC 0144 classed `extension` (brand, canvas, chat, coordination, dataIntegration, entities, kanban, knowledge, launchStudio, messaging, webResearch) — declared in neither the dotted nor the root spelling
entries.authority: v2 charter C.2 (RFC 0167 §E): one declaration file; extensions live under one namespaced key; RFC 0144 §A classified them deliberately as extension namespaces
entries.replacement: the v2 extension namespace key (C.2 child); the prose sections move to spec/v2/ext/
entries.note: Proposed: RFC 0144 chose not to declare these; the v2 C.2 child gives them a home under the single extension key rather than the open root.

entries.surface: the `/v1/` path-key prefix on every versioned operation
entries.authority: RFC 0172 §A.2 (v2 operations are unversioned path keys on a bare origin; v1 keys retained through the overlap and removed with the v1 tree at Phase 5)
entries.note: Proposed: the prefix is the v1 wire surface itself and cannot be deprecated inside v1.x; the row exists so the removal has a date and the alias coverage gate sees the surface.

entries.surface: the per-RFC `G<n>` local gap id as the register's ID column
entries.authority: RFC 0178 §B.2 (the `openwop.gap.<rfc>.<n>` id is canonical; `G<n>` is an alias until 2.1)
entries.note: Proposed: the alias survives through 2.0 so v1 register citations keep resolving; removed at 2.1.

entries.surface: registry version manifest `deprecated` boolean (an advisory version flag that collides with the JSON Schema `deprecated` annotation keyword)
entries.authority: RFC 0178 §A.1 (renamed so the annotation keyword is unambiguous); the rename rides C.10's registry/v2 re-sign
entries.note: Proposed: a wire field on signed, immutable manifests; the v2 manifest schema carries the new name and registry/v2 re-signs or overlays.

entries.surface: the two-segment interrupt resume token `base64url(payload).hmac` with no scheme id, algorithm, or key id
entries.authority: RFC 0170 §E.1 (`ow2.<alg>.<kid>.<payload>.<mac>`); interrupt.md §Resume tokens' rotation rule references an algorithm-version discriminator the format does not contain
entries.replacement: `ow2.<alg>.<kid>.<payload>.<mac>`; issued v1 tokens resolvable under `kid: legacy` until their expiry
entries.note: Proposed: a v1.x deprecation would need a new format to point at, which is the v2 change itself; the row exists so the removal has a date.

entries.surface: `details.retryAfter`, `details.retryAfterMs`, `details.retryAfterSeconds` on error envelopes (three body spellings beside the `Retry-After` header)
entries.authority: RFC 0171 §B.2 (retry timing lives in `Retry-After` only)
entries.note: Proposed: production-profile.md and scale-profiles.md MUST the body field equal the header; with the body field gone the header is the single source.

entries.surface: dotted reserved keys in `RunOptions.configurable` (`ai.provider`, `ai.model`, `ai.credentialRef`, `distillation.tokenBudget`) and the open map they live in
entries.authority: RFC 0171 §D.1 (closed, nested, versioned `configurable`)
entries.note: Proposed: the reserved `ai.*` namespace is a string prefix inside an open map; the v2 object nests it.

entries.surface: discovery flags that gate a security-load-bearing MUST: the fourteen `auth.*` gates, `replay.sideEffectSuppression`, `webhooks.durable`, `interrupt.approverRouting` (as a gate), `sandbox.supported` (as a gate)
entries.authority: RFC 0173 §A.1 (an obligation of the surface, never a discovery flag; RFC 0164 §22's ruling applied corpus-wide)
entries.replacement: the obligation binds when the surface is advertised; `auth.lanes[]`, `replay`, `webhooks`, `interrupt.refKinds[]`, `sandbox.isolationModel` stay as facets; relaxations are operator settings recorded in bundle v3 `host.relaxations[]`
entries.note: Proposed: each flag is a v1 advertisement an RFC minted; v2 removes the gating semantics with the flag.

entries.surface: `supportedTransports[]` at the discovery root (`rest | mcp | a2a | grpc`)
entries.authority: RFC 0175 §B.1 (REST is the wire; A2A and MCP are compositions with first-class facets; gRPC is demoted)
entries.note: Proposed: nothing in the corpus reads the `mcp` or `a2a` members (profiles.md reads only `rest`).

entries.surface: `capabilities.grpc` block and `grpc-transport.md` as a core Stable document with RFC 2119 MUSTs
entries.authority: RFC 0175 §A.1 (demoted to `spec/v2/ext/grpc-transport/`, `unwitnessable`, `adoption: none`; the door back into core is named)
entries.note: Proposed: the suite ships no gRPC client, no host advertises the block, and the proto defers its own messages to a v1.x that never landed.

sources.token: REST + SSE remains the REQUIRED wire surface

entries.surface: `/.well-known/wop` served byte-identically with `/.well-known/openwop` (MyndHyve, the wop → openwop rebrand alias; the C.5 precedent)
entries.note: Proposed: the alias exists in one host and was never registered; it is the model RFC 0172 cites for overlap publication.

entries.surface: `engines.openwop` ranges with no upper bound read as open (146 of 282 published versions)
entries.authority: RFC 0177 §A.1 (absent ceiling ⇒ `<2.0.0`; `pack_engine_unsupported` at install on every publication path)
entries.replacement: an explicit `>=x.y.z <M.0.0` range; the v2 schema enforces the grammar
entries.note: Proposed: no codemod — the author declares compatibility; `openwop.codemod.pack-manifest-v2` refuses a manifest with no v2-satisfiable range.

entries.surface: peer-dependency identifiers that are not declaration-file keys: `host.*` dotted twins (`host.fs`/`fs`, `host.queueBus`/`queueBus`), `openwop.agents.memoryBackends`, facet paths (`aiProviders.imageGeneration`, `host.aiEnvelope.await`), the reserved-slot prose list
entries.authority: RFC 0177 §B.1–§B.2 (identifier ≡ declaration-file key; `pack_peer_dependency_undefined` reads against the file; generated alias table)
entries.note: Proposed: the table is generated by `check-declaration.mjs` over the published manifests once the declaration file exists (RFC 0177 G2).

entries.surface: `signing.method: manual | ed25519 | sigstore` — two values the schema calls synonymous that the verifier treats as signatures over different bytes
entries.authority: RFC 0177 §C.3 (one `signing.scheme: ed25519-canonical-json`)
entries.note: Proposed: the codemod refuses `ed25519` and `sigstore` — those packs are re-signed in `registry/v2/`, never relabeled.

entries.surface: `connection-packs.md` clause 6: an installed pack takes precedence over a built-in of the same `provider.id` when its version is greater-than-or-equal
entries.authority: RFC 0177 §D.1 (RFC 0095 UQ4 decided: fail-closed `connection_provider_conflict`; qualified `<packName>#<id>` form)
entries.note: Proposed: silent precedence by version is the Axiom 2 failure UQ4 asked about.
